notes: Sample/demo config. In production this file is owned by the DRR/ops team and deployed independently of app code, per SRS Section 6 (Change Control) and FR-4.2. The active version string above is shown in the app footer for auditability.

terrain.notes: Elevation grid sampled from Open-Meteo's public elevation API (no key, no DEM file). reliefM = centre elevation minus the average of 8 ring points sampled sampleRadiusM metres out; negative = local bowl. slopePercent = steepest ring point vs centre, as a percent grade. A flat local bowl steps the tier up one; a steep, elevated spot steps it down one. See js/terrain.js for the full decision table.

waterProximity.notes: Nearest mapped river/stream/water body from OpenStreetMap (Overpass API), used as a positive-only signal: a feature within nearM steps the tier up one. No nearby feature found is treated as 'unknown', not 'safe', because OSM waterway coverage is incomplete in many rural areas. See js/waterway.js.

checklist.text: Fix the roof: loose sheets, missing nails, rusted ridges, and broken tiles.
Clear every drain, gutter, culvert, and trench you are responsible for. Wear gloves and closed boots.
Cut back trees over buildings, power lines, or places where children play. Use a professional for large limbs or trees near power lines.
Walk your evacuation route in daylight and at night with the whole household or team.
Ask three long-term neighbours how high floodwater has reached and mark that line on a wall.
Protect your water source: raise and cover well and borehole heads and prevent contamination from latrines or animal pens.
List people who need help to move and assign a named helper to each one.
Refill 30 days of chronic medicines, including blood pressure, diabetes, epilepsy, ARVs, TB, and mental-health medication.
Service the vehicle, generator, water pump, and boat. Fuel up and test-run the generator under load.
Photograph IDs, title deeds, birth certificates, school records, and medical records and store copies outside the flood zone.
Have raincoats, umbrellas, gumboots, buckets, and zip-lock bags ready.
Assemble a 72-hour supply kit with waterproofed clothes, food, water, medicines, sanitary needs, and cleaning items.
Fill and seal drinking-water reserves: at least 3 litres per person per day for 3 days.
Buy water-treatment supplies such as chlorine tablets or solution, or fuel for boiling.
Get a torch and a battery or wind-up radio.
Charge power banks, buy phone credit, and keep mobile-money access plus small-denomination cash.
Put passports, deeds, certificates, and exam slips in a sealed plastic bag or box.
Restock the first-aid kit and add ORS sachets and zinc for children.
Hang or repair mosquito nets now.
Set up a communication tree and choose one out-of-area relative for network failures.
Agree two meeting points: one just outside the house and one on high ground outside the neighbourhood.
For livestock, identify high ground, arrange fodder, mark animals, and agree who will move them.
Businesses and schools: decide the closure trigger in writing and tell everyone what it is.
